title: Photovoltaic power stations enhanced ecosystem multifunctionality while maintaining stable plant diversity with time on the Qinghai‐Xizang Plateau
content:
These results indicate that the operation of PV power stations drives a continuous improvement in regional EMF, with no adverse impacts on local biodiversity that remains at a stable level. The deployment of PV power stations confers long-term ecological restoration benefits to alpine grasslands, underscoring the environmental compatibility and inherent sustainability of PV power stations in these ecologically sensitive regions.


Abstract

Large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power stations on the ecologically fragile Qinghai-Xizang Plateau (QXP) have raised critical widespread concerns, as alpine grasslands are pivotal biodiversity hotspots and provide core ecosystem services that underpin ecological security on the QXP. While PV power stations have been widely implemented as a key strategy for clean energy transition and climate change mitigation, a critical knowledge gap remains regarding the long-term impacts of PV operations on alpine grassland plant diversity and ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF). Here, we conducted a field investigation across 8 PV arrays with operation periods ranging from 1 to 12 years in the Talatan PV Park. We classified sampling plots into three zones: under-panel, inter-panel and unaffected control zones, and identified the driving factors of alpine grassland EMF using random forest models and structural equation models. PV-affected zones showed significantly higher vegetation growth, soil nutrient contents, soil moisture and overall EMF than the unaffected control zones, with only minor differences detected between the two PV zones. EMF increased markedly and continuously along the PV operational chronosequence, whereas plant diversity showed no consistent temporal trend. PV operational age was the dominant driver of EMF, with plant diversity (regulatory threshold of 0.61) and soil moisture serving as key mediating variables. Synthesis and applications. These results indicate that the operation of PV power stations drives a continuous improvement in regional EMF, with no adverse impacts on local biodiversity that remains at a stable level. The deployment of PV power stations confers long-term ecological restoration benefits to alpine grasslands, underscoring the environmental compatibility and inherent sustainability of PV power stations in these ecologically sensitive regions.
